title: Automating hESC differentiation with 3D printing and legacy liquid handling solutions
author: Zluhan, Kelly, et al.

steps.title: Design and print custom tools
steps.instruction: Create 3‑D models of a 6‑position cell scraper and a disposable filter box using Google SketchUp®, export as .stl files, and print them on a MakerBot Replicator® 2 with white PLA (or ABS) filament.

substeps.instruction: Design scraper to fit each well of a 6‑well plate (6 positions).
Design filter box in three sections: a 155 mL main reservoir, two ~35 mL side reservoirs for PBS and Accutase, and a holster for a micro‑centrifuge tube.
Export models as .stl files for printing.

steps.title: Coat and sterilize printed items
steps.instruction: Apply a waterproof sealant (epoxy resin, silicone, or acetone‑treated ABS) to the printed parts, then sterilize by UV light before use; discard the filter box after a single use.

substeps.instruction: If using PLA, coat with epoxy or silicone.
If using ABS, treat with acetone to melt layers and make liquid‑proof.

steps.title: Calibrate robot and pipette
steps.instruction: Perform full robot calibration (arm x‑, y‑, z‑axes, gripper, and pipette) before recording movement scripts and before running any protocol.

steps.title: Verify robot performance (optional)
steps.instruction: Run a test protocol with an inexpensive cell line such as HEK 293 to confirm pipetting accuracy and cell‑culture handling before using hESCs.

steps.title: Seed starter hESC cultures
steps.instruction: Manually seed two wells of hESC line ES‑701 (BioTime, USA) onto Synthemax‑coated 6‑well plates (CLS3978, Sigma‑Aldrich) using mTeSR‑1 medium.

steps.title: Grow cells to confluence
steps.instruction: Incubate the starter cultures until they reach 70–80 % confluence.

steps.title: Program robot for cell passaging
steps.instruction: Create a Bioworks movement script that (a) uses the gripper to pick up the 6‑position cell scraper and scrape each well, then (b) moves the pipette to the four corners of each well for trituration to detach cells, and (c) transfers cells from the original 2 wells to a total of 6 wells, yielding 2 new starter wells and 4 wells for monocyte differentiation.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate and dispense at four corners for trituration.

steps.title: Transfer embryoid bodies
steps.instruction: Using the robot’s 8‑channel pipette, dispense 16 embryoid bodies (instead of the original 20) from each 96‑well plate into each well of a 6‑well plate for monocyte differentiation.

steps.title: Manually centrifuge 96‑well plates
steps.instruction: Since the robot lacks a centrifuge, remove the 96‑well plates after embryoid‑body formation and centrifuge them manually according to the Wilgenburg protocol.

steps.title: Filter cells with custom box
steps.instruction: Place the filter box on the robot work surface; use the pipette to dispense cell suspensions through the filter into the 155 mL main reservoir, draw PBS and Accutase from the ~35 mL side reservoirs for washes and enzymatic detachment, and collect an aliquot in the micro‑centrifuge tube holster for cell‑counting.

substeps.instruction: Load PBS and Accutase into their respective chambers.
Dispense cells through filter into main reservoir.

steps.title: Proceed with monocyte differentiation
steps.instruction: Continue the remaining steps of the Wilgenburg et al. monocyte differentiation protocol (media changes, incubation times, etc.) using the robot as programmed, following the established schedule.
